previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, prior CABG, and osteoporosis was admitted for acute onset midsternal chest pain at rest, lasting two hours and relieved with nitroglycerin. Initial evaluation showed no EKG changes or elevated troponins. A pharmacological stress test revealed normal myocardial perfusion and no ischemia, with a high ejection fraction likely overestimated due to small cavity size. She was diagnosed with unstable angina and started on atorvastatin 20 mg daily. Chronic issues including hypothyroidism, GERD, restless legs syndrome, and osteoporosis were managed with home medications. Home physical therapy was arranged for continued support. She was discharged home with follow-up planned with her primary care provider.
problems: Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery with unstable angina pectoris
Age-related osteoporosis without current pathological fracture
